sources.entry: Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol servers.

summary.name: XMPP
summary.one_liner: XMPP (Extensible Messaging and Presence Protocol, originally Jabber) is an open, XML-based, federated protocol for instant messaging, presence and contact lists.
use_cases: running a private federated chat server
chatting with users on other servers
voice and video calls over an open protocol
bridging other chat networks through gateways
summary.what_it_does: XMPP is an open XML-based protocol for instant messaging, presence and contact lists, standardized by the IETF in RFCs 6120 and 6121. Anyone can run their own server, and users are addressed with email-like Jabber IDs, so servers federate much like SMTP email. The protocol is extended through XMPP Extension Protocols (XEPs) covering features such as multi-user chat, file upload, voice and video via Jingle, and service discovery. Gateways can connect XMPP users to other networks such as ICQ, AIM, IRC or SMS.
notable: Federated, decentralized design similar to email, with Jabber IDs like alice@example.com
Extensible through XEPs, including multi-user chat, Jingle VoIP and OMEMO end-to-end encryption
Gateways (transports) bridge to ICQ, AIM, Yahoo, IRC, SMS and email
caveats: Plain XML text causes higher network overhead than binary protocols
In-band binary transfer is limited, so file transfers rely on out-of-band mechanisms such as HTTP File Upload
Several large vendors dropped or limited XMPP support over time (e.g., Google Talk federation, AIM, Facebook chat)
